Jarvis 0.15.2

Take a task with you. Everything a task knows — the ask, who made it, what the deadline is, the messages it came out of — could be read on screen but never carried anywhere. Now one press copies the lot.

Copy a task and its context

  • Open a task and the top bar carries a copy button, beside the owl. It puts the whole task on the clipboard as plain Markdown: the title, who asked and when it is due, why it is a task, the next step, and every message it was read out of — each under its conversation, with the link back.
  • Paste it into a coding agent, another assistant, a document or a message to a colleague. Nothing has to be retyped.
  • A citation Jarvis cannot read right now — offline, outside the conversations you chose, or rate limited — copies as its timestamp and link, exactly as the screen shows it.

No change to what leaves your Mac: Slack is still searched live and never stored, and mail and meetings stay on your machine. Copying writes nothing to disk — the words go to your clipboard because you asked for them.

Jarvis 0.15.1

A task Jarvis found, and then quietly dropped. Two fixes: one recovers work that was being lost between deciding and telling you, the other makes the app say what it can be clicked.

Tasks that were found and then lost

  • When Jarvis weighed a message, decided it was yours, and then failed to list it, nothing caught the contradiction — the task simply never appeared, with no sign anywhere that it had been found. Jarvis now notices and asks itself again before finishing the run.
  • Someone naming you in a channel is choosing you out of everyone there, so a direct mention that asks a question, reports a problem, or requests something now counts as yours unless the conversation shows it was already answered.
  • A task you already marked done is never reopened by this.

The pointer

  • Everything clickable now shows the hand cursor — your tasks on the day, the messages behind a task, the buttons in a task, and controls across the Hub, meetings, settings and the notes log.
  • A control with nothing to open keeps the plain arrow, so the hand always means a click will do something.

No change to what leaves your Mac: Slack is still searched live and never stored, and mail and meetings stay on your machine.

Jarvis 0.15.0

See what a task came from, and tell Jarvis how to rank it. Two additions: a task now shows you the messages behind it, and a note you type can become a standing rule that changes what Jarvis treats as urgent.

The messages behind a task

  • Open a task and "Where this came from" now shows the messages themselves — who wrote them, when, and what they said — instead of a bare timestamp link. Slack markup is rendered readable, so a mention reads as a name and a link reads as its label.
  • The words are fetched from Slack when you open the task and held only while the app is running. Nothing is written to your disk, and disconnecting Slack clears them immediately.
  • The arrow on any message still opens it at the source, and a note you told Jarvis now opens your notes log rather than doing nothing.
  • If Slack is disconnected or unreachable, a task looks exactly as it did before — the link is still there, only the words are missing.
  • "How Jarvis found this" is gone; the same run is one click away from the owl at the top of a task.

House rules

  • Press ⌘K, tick "Treat this as a rule", and tell Jarvis something like "anything Dana asks me for comes before everything else". The task moves immediately — no sync, no waiting for the next run.
  • A task moved by one of your rules says so: its priority reads "your rule", and opening it quotes the rule that did it, with a way to stop using it.
  • Every rule lives in your Told Jarvis log, and stopping one puts the task back where it was.

Fixes

  • The current-time marker on your day no longer has its clock cut off.
  • A task whose next step came back as runaway repeated text is repaired, and Jarvis now refuses to store that kind of output in the first place.
  • Long notes no longer push a task off its own screen.
  • Citations that pointed nowhere are no longer shown.

No change to what leaves your Mac: Slack is still searched live and never stored, and mail and meetings stay on your machine.
